title: HTTP Verb
body:
The method on an [[HTTP]] request, stating what kind of operation it is. The client chooses it; the server must have a handler registered for that method on that path, or it answers 404 (no such path) or 405 (wrong method for this path).

| Verb | Meaning | Safe? | [[Idempotent]]? |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | Read a resource | Yes | Yes |
| POST | Create something | No | No |
| PUT | Replace a resource entirely | No | Yes |
| PATCH | Update part of a resource | No | Not guaranteed |
| DELETE | Remove a resource | No | Yes |
| HEAD | Like GET, headers only, no body | Yes | Yes |
| OPTIONS | "What am I allowed to send?" | Yes | Yes |

*Safe* means no side effects at all; *idempotent* means doing it repeatedly has the same effect as doing it once. OPTIONS is special in that your JS never writes it — the browser generates it automatically as a [[Preflight Request]]. Choosing verbs to match resource nouns is the core of [[REST]].
